question: **Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank no. 2.**
solution:
The correct answer is "**sleeping**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the given sentence, we need to use" **sleeping" **in the present participle form.
 
• Now, this might sound slightly confusing since usually when we use was (indicative of past tense), we tend to use the past tense of the verb or past participle form.
 
• In the given sentence, we are using "was" as an **auxiliary verb **followed by using the progressive/**present participle form** of the verb(ing form).
 
• In the given sentence, by using was as an **auxiliary **verb and the present participle of the main verb "**sleeping**", the given sentence becomes **past continuous tense**.
 
• It is common to use **past continuous tense **when we are narrating the background of a story just like in the given passage.
 
• The given passage is narrating the story of a robbery in which the person ends up injuring himself.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **option 4.**

 

**The complete passage is**: Recently, there was a news report about a man who tried to catch a robber but suffered a hip **(1)fracture** in the process. The victim was a plumber and he was **(2)sleeping** in the hall outside the bedroom. He had left the bedroom door open for better ventilation. **(3)About** two hours after midnight, he heard some noise from the bedroom. When he went in to check, he found a man **(4)breaking** open the cupboard and taking away jewellery and cash. On seeing him, the robber tried to escape and jumped from the second floor. The plumber **(5)chased** the robber and jumped after him. Unfortunately, he hit a concrete wall and broke his hip; he was rushed to a nearby hospital. The robber managed to escape.
